answer.exemplar: A load-bearing wall must be deep enough to carry the weight of what stands above it and to resist the pushes of the vaults and roof, and a wall of that kind can only be pierced by small openings. questions.explanation: A load-bearing wall can only take small openings, but a frame carries the loads instead, leaving the wall as a thin skin that can be largely glazed. The frame sets the window size free.
